- Market / segment (low risk, from our winners): nurses on back-to-back 12-hour shifts. Iteration of our top healthcare winner TOFv1_HF2 | 807_Aubrey "Don't Waste Spent Money" ($1,720, ROAS 1.72, last 7 days).
- Avatar: woman, 35-55, American RN, works three or four 12s in a row on hospital floors, mom, has spent years and hundreds of dollars on "nurse shoes" that failed; persona "The Shift Survivor" (avatar_personas.md Persona 1).
- Her language (from the winner and nurse forums): "12s", "three 12s in a row", "my feet are done by hour 8", "Hokas", "Brooks", "Danskos", "my closet of shoes", "rotate between 2 pairs".
- Topic (behavior research this week): nurses say Hokas feel "wobbly" standing still and fall short on long days (allnurses.com threads); a 2026 podiatrist guide says if your feet hurt more at the end of a shift than the start, the cushioning is bottoming out, and shoes fine at hour 2 hurt by hour 10 as feet swell (michiganfootdoctors.com); many nurses carry a second pair and switch mid-shift.
- Angle / habit she has today: buying another $150-$200 pair of running shoes every few months because "that's what nurses wear", and switching pairs halfway through the shift.
- Point of contact (what she and our winning nurse ads already blame): her shoes, and the hard hospital floors. Confirm it.
- Problem mechanism (connect dots she already half-believes): running shoes are built for forward motion and short bursts, not standing and walking on hard floors for 12 hours; their soft foam arch flattens partway through the shift; her feet swell through the day so a shoe that fit at 7 AM pinches by the afternoon. (Source: the 807 winner's own script + the podiatrist guide.)
- Function mechanism (why the fix she tried works for others but not her): Hokas and Brooks work for runners on a 45-minute run; she is on her feet for 12 hours on tile. What she needs is support that is still there at hour 10, room that gives when feet swell, and grip for hospital floors, all at once.
- Solution mechanism: Ortho Stretch puts those in one shoe: built-in arch support with a cushioned rocker sole, a stretch-knit upper with a wide toe box that gives as feet swell, a slip-resistant sole, no-tie stretch laces.
- Conditions (her do-it-yourself fixes and why they miss): sizing up makes the heel slip; insoles take up the toe room in an already narrow shoe; clogs don't give; a second pair mid-shift just swaps one problem for another.
- USP: the conditions above, met in one shoe, at $59.95.
- Features with the lever each pulls: arch support + rocker sole (odds: still there at hour 10); stretch knit + wide toe box (dream: feet that aren't screaming when she gets home); slip-resistant sole (odds/safety: a must on hospital floors, per the winner); no-tie laces (effort).
- Dream (identity, not "no pain"): getting through three 12s in a row and still having the energy to be mom when she gets home.
- Time: no break-in timeline is confirmed; don't promise one or "instant relief". A real nurse quote from the winner: "worn them up to 4 12s in a row at the ER with zero pain" (Emily, RN; use only as her words).
- Anchoring: $59.95 vs the $150-$200 running shoes in her closet that died in two months; "so affordable if you're living on nurse wages" (winner's testimonial).
- Risk reversal: 30-day money-back guarantee = a full refund within 30 days; that's about 12 of her shifts to prove it on her own feet. Never say "easy returns".
- Gain now: Black Friday: 60% OFF SITEWIDE + BUY 2 PAIRS, GET 2 FREE GIFTS. Many nurses rotate 2 pairs (our winner's testimonial: "I rotate between 2 pairs"), so buying two is natural.
- Lose later: the Black Friday price. The sale's end date is NOT confirmed and stock is NOT confirmed: no dates, no "selling out".
- Risk: moderate, 1 bet = the F31 creator-review format (new to our account, proven for Cuurt). Market, segment and mechanism come from our winner.

CLAIMS: approved: 30-day money-back guarantee, 500,000+, HSA/FSA eligible, doctor-recommended, podiatrist-recommended. Never: "orthopedic approved", cure/treatment claims (no "fixes plantar fasciitis"), named or counted doctors, extra-wide or fits-everyone promises, instant relief, shipping speed, star ratings or review counts, "easy returns". Not confirmed: B-width, EU tooling, half sizes.
